title: Zig — Allocators, comptime & Error Unions
description: Core Zig: explicit allocation, comptime, error unions and optionals, defer, and the no-hidden-control-flow philosophy.

questions.prompt: A core Zig design principle is 'no hidden control flow and no hidden ___'.
questions.explanation: Allocation is always explicit via an allocator you pass in; nothing allocates behind your back.

questions.prompt: In Zig, heap allocation is performed by:

options: An explicit std.mem.Allocator passed to the code

questions.explanation: Functions that allocate take an Allocator parameter, making ownership and strategy explicit and testable.

questions.prompt: Zig's comptime executes ordinary Zig code at compile time, and is how generics are implemented.
questions.explanation: Types are values at comptime; generic functions take comptime type parameters rather than a separate template language.

questions.prompt: Zig ships with a built-in garbage collector.
questions.explanation: Zig has no GC; memory is managed manually through explicit allocators (often paired with defer).

questions.prompt: A Zig error union type is written as:
questions.explanation: `!T` is an error-set-or-value union; you resolve it with try, catch, or if/else capture.

questions.prompt: Which Zig keyword propagates an error union's error up to the caller (returning early on error)?
questions.explanation: `try expr` returns the error if expr is an error, otherwise yields the unwrapped value.

questions.prompt: Zig represents a possibly-absent value (an optional) with the type syntax:
questions.explanation: `?T` is an optional; unwrap with `orelse`, `if (x) |v|`, or `.?`.

questions.prompt: A `defer` statement in Zig runs its expression:
questions.explanation: defer schedules cleanup at scope exit (errdefer only on error paths) — the idiomatic free-after-alloc pattern.

questions.prompt: Zig's ReleaseSafe and Debug builds insert runtime checks for things like integer overflow and out-of-bounds access.
questions.explanation: Safety-checked builds trap on detectable undefined behavior; ReleaseFast/Small drop the checks for speed/size.

questions.prompt: Explain how Zig's explicit-allocator approach helps prevent memory leaks and makes code more testable, contrasting it with a hidden global allocator.

payload.rubric: Notes allocator passed as a parameter (caller controls strategy/lifetime); pairing with defer for deterministic free; std.testing.allocator detecting leaks in tests.
